mechaber.1#main: The law of not sticking dough on unsalted meat. In it is one seif: One who coats with dough — a bird that was not salted — even though in the Gemara they distinguish between semolina and other flours and between thin dough (asmik) and dough that is not thin, we nowadays are not expert in the matter, and in every case one should forbid; but if it was salted and remained for the time of salting and afterward was rinsed, it is permitted in every manner: {Rama: And specifically coating with dough is forbidden, but one may smear with oil or meat juice on unsalted meat, for this does not impede exudation (Arukh general rule 9). And pashtida has every law of cooking in a pot, both for leniency and for stringency (Mordechai chapter 25 in the name of Rashi and Mahari and Arukh general rule 15):}

siftei-kohen.1#א: ["One who coats, etc. — meaning at the time of roasting; investigate. And this coating is not the pashtida that the Rav wrote, for pashtida is forbidden by Torah law as we see that they do not exude from the place where they sit dry in the oven; rather it is what they were accustomed to smear on dough whose batter is soft, and they were accustomed to do around gizzards and intestines that they place on the spit and coat around them with soft dough — so wrote Tosafot, Agudah, Mordechai chapter 25, Semag, and other poskim; if so, for us who are not expert in the matter, even coating with dough whose batter is soft has every law of cooking in a pot, both for leniency and for stringency, as the Taz wrote:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ב: ["And pashtida, etc. — language of Tur HaChadash general rule 28 seif 2: and pashtida has the law of cooking, and we estimate with sixty, both for leniency and for stringency — that if there is sixty everything is permitted except that piece to which the prohibition adheres, and if there is not sixty everything is forbidden — end of his words:"]

turei-zahav.1#א: Or meat juice on unsalted meat. Explanation: meat juice is permitted to smear on unsalted meat, and this juice is meat juice; and in Or Zarua he wrote seasoned eggs and juice is not mentioned there.
turei-zahav.1#ב: Both for leniency and for stringency. Explanation: we estimate with sixty and discard that piece and the rest is permitted, and we do not say we are concerned that perhaps at first two or three pieces became forbidden through fat that dripped there at first and would require sixty against those two or three pieces — we do not say so.

baer-heitev.1#א: In every case. Shach wrote: even coating with dough whose batter is soft has every law of cooking in a pot, both for leniency and for stringency.
baer-heitev.1#ב: Juice. Explanation: juice — it is permitted to smear on unsalted meat, and this juice is meat juice; and in Or Zarua he wrote seasoned eggs and juice is not mentioned there.
baer-heitev.1#ג: And pashtida. Explanation: if they roasted pashtida on coals or in a pan and found in it liver or heart, its law is like cooking — if there is sixty everything is permitted except the liver or heart or the piece to which the prohibition adheres, and if there is not sixty everything is forbidden (and see Peri Chadash).
baer-heitev.1#ד: For leniency. Explanation: if there is sixty in it everything is permitted except that piece to which the prohibition adheres, and if there is not sixty everything is forbidden; and Taz wrote we do not say we are concerned that perhaps at first two or three pieces became forbidden through fat that dripped there at first and would require sixty against those pieces — we do not say so, end of his words.

beer-hagolah.1#ב: Shibolei HaLeket; and Beit Yosef wrote that perhaps for this reason Rif and Rosh omitted it.

beur-hagra.1#א: But if, etc. — as the view of all the commentators that the entire sugya is regarding unsalted meat, not like Rambam; and see above siman 69 seif 19.
beur-hagra.1#ב: But permitted, etc. — as written there 70b: anoint with oil, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ג: And pashtida, etc. — Tosafot there 74b s.v. tafel; and more.
beur-hagra.1#ד: Both, etc. — Or Zarua, not like Rabbenu Baruch; and so appears to me.

kereti.1#א: On a bird — not specifically a bird; the same applies to a limb from an animal per the Gemara's law; only the Tanna used "bird" because even though its blood is slight, it still requires conditions.
kereti.1#ב: In every case one should forbid — even a bird, and even though a bird exudes and what difference does it make regarding a bird in coating as implied from Rashi — nevertheless it is forbidden because we are concerned the flour will clump if it is not so thin and will prevent exudation from the bird; and for us who hold chanan, if so the coating is chanan and forbids the bird, and ein hana'asur does not apply here — perhaps it absorbs something.
kereti.1#ג: And afterward rinsed, etc. — this is obvious; what concern is there that it will exude its blood? Rambam is stringent because he holds all meat requires scalding in boiling water; but for us who do not require scalding, this is superfluous language.
kereti.1#ד: And pashtida, etc. — and Peri Chadash disagrees; one should not depart from what Rama said in a rabbinic matter.

kaf-hachayim.1#_: (1) [Seif 1] One who coats with dough on an unsalted bird. Time of salting. Tur and Beit Yosef. Leket Yosher. But if it was salted and remained for the time of salting and afterward was rinsed, it is permitted in every manner as written afterward in Shulchan Aruch; and so Bach.

rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.1#_: (Siman 78 seif 1 in the hagahah) Or meat juice on unsalted meat. See Taz above seif 65 and in Ba'er Hetev there in the name of the Gaon EH z"l.
